title: Original-stage inclusion of a realized point diagram
statement: Fix finite-field datum D, prime l different from its characteristic, an algebraic closure Omega of Q_l and a finite coefficient stage F. Put E=Coefficient(l,Omega,F). For any category I, E-module diagram V, operators A_i, and an already realized rational heart diagram G with natural Weil and fibre isomorphisms theta and eta and transport isomorphisms t satisfying ZlPointDiagramRealization of [def-zl-point-equivariant-diagram-realization], the predicate ZlCommonStageDiagram(D,l,hl,Omega,F,V,A,G,theta,eta,t) holds. Its objects are the literal inclusions at F, lie in the common-stage heart and realize the scalar-extended relations, monos, short exact sequences and cokernels. The natural isomorphisms and point transport satisfy the specified stage-pullback, stage-fibre and transport-square comparisons; the conjugated Frobenius and inverse Weil maps are the scalar extensions of A and its inverse. There is no enlargement of F and no new existence-of-original-diagram assertion.

proof.text: At $\Omega$ take exactly the common-stage images $(E,M_i)$ and maps represented by the already constructed $E$-maps [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients; def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. Every relation and both inverse identities already hold at $E$, so hold in the common-stage category without any enlargement. By [prop-constructible-truncations] the stagewise truncations keep these images in the $\Omega$-heart; their degree-zero fibres and comparisons are the scalar extensions in [lem-zl-point-heart-finite-stage]. Extension of vector spaces is exact by [lem-weil-field-scalar-extension-exact], and the exact $\Omega$-heart equivalence of [lem-zl-point-heart-finite-stage] reflects the resulting short exact sequences and cokernels. The scalar transport compatibility just used, including its common-stage form [lem-weil-frobenius-point-transport-natural](2), identifies their Frobenius with $A_i\otimes_E\Omega$. The object at $i_*$ is exactly the common-stage image of the prescribed object, with its prescribed comparison. Everything is defined over the original $E$, uniformly for any finite-field datum.
